English: South Wind Prayer
Chinese: 南风祈祷

English: The chimes proclaiming South Wind's Prayer echoed through the wide boulevards and gardens of the Imperial City, calling all to their temples. The Emperor Reman III always attended a service at the Temple of the One, while his son and heir Prince Juilek found it more political to attend a service at a different temple for each religious holiday. This year, it was at the cathedral Benevolence of Mara. # The chimes proclaiming South Wind's Prayer echoed through the wide boulevards and gardens of the Imperial City, calling all to their temples. The Emperor Reman III always attended a service at the Temple of the One, while his son and heir Prince Juilek found it more political to attend a service at a different temple for each religious holiday. This year, it was at the cathedral Benevolence of Mara.
Chinese: 宣布南风祈祷的钟声回荡在帝都宽阔的林荫道与花园之间,召唤所有人前往神殿。雷曼三世皇帝总是去独一神殿参加仪式,而他的儿子、继承人朱莱克王子则认为,每个宗教节日轮流去不同的神殿更有政治益处。今年,是玛拉仁慈大教堂。#宣布南风祈祷的钟声回荡在帝都宽阔的林荫道与花园之间,召唤所有人前往神殿。雷曼三世皇帝总是去独一神殿参加仪式,而他的儿子、继承人朱莱克王子则认为,每个宗教节日轮流去不同的神殿更有政治益处。今年,是玛拉仁慈大教堂。

English: On Wikkan Tyranny, by Nelio Conicus - 1436
Chinese: 论维坎暴政,内利奥·科尼库斯著——1436

English: There was a time, before the God War, when every human settlement on these flying isles was built around a Wikkan coven. From Vena to Slev they enforced worship, demanding prayer to their gods. And so did those old gods grow in power once more, under the flag of Wikkan tyranny. ##That the Apostatic Union succeeded in overthrowing this tyranny - in casting down those gods - is a miracle worth celebrating. I am old enough to remember Wikkan rule. Every spell, every letter of cipher was controlled by the covens. What magic was permitted changed from realm to realm, as each coven's god had its own fickle whims. Not since the Middle Ages, when gods ruled supreme, has human development been so stunted. ##And since the Union gained its freedom, look at the advances we have made; airships soar through the clouds! Lowly scribes cast spells of swiftness and strength! Our cities throb with wealth and progress! No longer must we barter with gods for the merest enchantment; humanity rules its destiny, like the Emberians of the past. ##And yet, there are those in our midst who would see it all torn down. Outside Union borders, the Wikkans and their gods are more powerful than ever. Their spies and priests still lurk in every corner of the Union - some even hidden and protected by our own traitorous citizens! And despite these dangers, what do we discuss in our councils? Reform? Softer punishments for god worship? I call this foolishness of the highest regard. ##Many know of Beatrice Webb - she has made quite a name for herself here in Riova. She attests that our methods are too harsh. That god worship should be punished with a mere fine, and that censure of texts should be ended - bringing about a 'freedom of the quill'. ##I argue that such things would, in no uncertain terms, bring about the destruction of the Apostatic Union. It is only by a hair's breadth that we can stay ahead of our many enemies; the Wikkans would see our realms torn apart, our magical progress abolished and the rule of the gods reinstated. Nay, our punishments are not too harsh, they are too soft. I would see Wikkan sympathisers hung before I bow to another god. I am old enough to remember Wikkan tyranny, and I would die before I see it reinstated.
Chinese: 神之战以前,曾有一段时光,这些飞行岛屿上每一处人类聚落都围绕着一座维坎女巫团而建。从维纳到斯列夫,他们强制崇拜,索要对其神明的祈祷。于是,在维坎暴政的旗帜下,那些古老的神再度壮大。##叛教联盟成功推翻这一暴政——打倒那些神明——是一个值得庆祝的奇迹。我年纪够大,记得维坎的统治。每一道咒语、每一个密文字母,都由女巫团掌控。什么魔法获准使用,因国而异,因为每位神各有其反复无常的癖性。自中世纪诸神至高无上的年代以来,人类的发展从未如此迟滞。##而自从联盟赢得自由,看看我们取得的进步吧;飞艇穿云而过!卑贱的书记员也能施放迅捷与力量之法!我们的城市因财富与进步而搏动!再也不必为最微小的附魔与神明讨价还价;人类掌握自己的命运,一如昔日的余烬人。##然而,我们中间仍有人想把这一切拆个粉碎。联盟边界之外,维坎人和他们的神比以往更强大。他们的间谍和祭司仍潜伏在联盟的每个角落——有些甚至藏在我们自己叛国公民的庇护之下!尽管危机重重,我们在议事会上讨论的又是什么?改革?减轻对神明崇拜的惩罚?我说这是最高级别的愚蠢。##许多人都知道比阿特丽斯·韦伯——她在里奥瓦已小有名气。她声称我们的手段太严酷。说神明崇拜应当仅处罚款,还说应当终止对文本的审查——带来一种"执笔自由"。##我要申明,这些主张毫不含糊地会带来叛教联盟的毁灭。我们领先众多敌人,只差毫厘;维坎人巴不得我们的国土四分五裂,我们的魔法进步付诸东流,诸神的统治卷土重来。不,我们的惩罚不是太严酷,而是太仁慈。在我向另一位神低头之前,我宁愿看到维坎同情者被绞死。我年纪够大,记得维坎的暴政,我宁可先死,也不愿见它重演。

English: The Tragedy of King Tristwich, by Joan Toussaint - 1213
Chinese: 特里斯维奇王悲剧,琼·图森著——1213

English: Though the bodies are buried thus ending our war,#Weep, weep for Tristwich, for none have lost more.'##So goes a rhyme from the War of Weeping, in the middle ages. A time before the World Rend, before the golden age of the Emberians. A time when castles rose high and kings were bound to patron gods. ##King Tristwich ruled Thwyf, a surface-kingdom now lost. He was tied by ceremony to Paeguth, a god of growth and long-life. Tristwich bore these gifts plainly; there are accounts that at the age of one-hundred, he still bore the face of a man not thirty winters old. His kingdom flourished; each harvest was more bountiful than the last, and the people rejoiced.##But any god-contract bears a cost. In those early years such burdens were subtle; Tristwich could not conceive an heir. He ruled in sadness, old in mind yet young in body, and he outlived his wife.##When his grief subsided, he adopted a daughter; a war-orphan, Obaith. As she grew, it kindled a love in Tristwich like he had never known. In time, Obaith fell in love with a prince from a neighbouring kingdom; and the magnificent marriage would forever unite the two realms. ##The ceremony was exquisite, the vows poetic. But as the betrothed shared a gentle kiss, crimson spilled forth. Their last breath was shared and they both fell down dead. For the prince's patron god was Elswyn; a god of love, but also of war. This was not a marriage, but a declaration.##The fields of Thwyf were stained with blood. Neighbouring kingdoms joined the conflict, and soon the whole continent was at war. Not before or since have so many lost their lives; for it is said that every family in every realm knew grief. Thus it was known as the War of Weeping.##Paeguth blessed the warriors of Thwyf with strength, but his love was tainted with pain - and his warriors became monstrous. As the war raged, kings and gods alike were slain, their kingdoms lost. ##On the dawn of the sixtieth summer, Thwyf's last stronghold was besieged. Elswyn stormed the castle-keep herself, and slew the bloated, monstrous form that Paeguth had become... though some say an aspect of him escaped. ##What became of Tristwich, the old books do not say -  though an old wive's tale persists. It was said, on the moonlit fields of Thwyf, a strange man could sometimes be seen. He would stumble forth, calling the name of Obaith, tears streaming from youthful eyes.
Chinese: 纵然尸骸已葬,战争就此终结,#哭吧,为特里斯维奇哭吧,无人失去得更多。'##哭泣之战的一首童谣如此唱道,在中世纪。那是在世界撕裂之前,余烬人的黄金时代之前。城堡高耸、君王系于守护神的年代。##特里斯维奇王统治着斯威夫,一个如今已失落的地上王国。他依礼制与帕古斯相连,一位生长与长寿之神。特里斯维奇明显带着这些恩赐;据记载,他一百岁时,面容仍似不满三十岁的青年。他的王国欣欣向荣;一年收成胜过一年,人民欢欣鼓舞。##但凡神之契约,必有代价。早年间这负担还很隐晦;特里斯维奇无法孕育继承人。他在悲伤中统治,心智已老,身体犹少,他送走了自己的妻子。##悲恸平复之后,他收养了一个女儿;战争孤儿,奥贝丝。随着她长大,一种特里斯维奇从未体味过的爱在他心中燃起。后来,奥贝丝与邻国的一位王子相爱;这场盛大的婚礼将永远联结两个王国。##仪式精美绝伦,誓词诗意盎然。但当新人温柔相吻时,猩红迸溅。他们共享了最后一次呼吸,双双倒地而亡。因为王子的守护神是艾尔温;一位爱之神,也是战之神。这不是一场婚礼,而是一份宣战。##斯威夫的田野浸透了鲜血。邻国纷纷卷入冲突,很快整个大陆陷入战争。空前绝后,这么多生灵涂炭;据说每个国度的每个家庭都尝过丧亲之痛。因此它被称为哭泣之战。##帕古斯赐予斯威夫战士力量,但他的爱掺着痛苦——他的战士变得畸形怪异。战火蔓延,君王与神明纷纷殒命,他们的王国随之失落。##第六十个夏天的黎明,斯威夫最后的堡垒被围。艾尔温亲自攻入城堡主楼,杀死了帕古斯变成的肿胀怪异的形态……尽管有人说,他的一缕面相逃了出去。##特里斯维奇的下场,古书没有记载——只有一个老太婆故事流传至今。据说,在斯威夫月光照耀的田野上,有时能看见一个奇怪的男人。他踉跄前行,呼唤着奥贝丝的名字,年轻的眼中泪水长流。

English: The World Rend, by Joan Toussant - 1206
Chinese: 世界撕裂,琼·图森著——1206

English: The World Rend. Though it has long passed into distant memory, it is still spoken of in hushed tones by nervous speakers. For who cannot still dread the cataclysm that levelled our cities, purged our wisdom and sent us fleeing to the sky? ##There are none alive who remember stable ground underfoot. Generations have lived and died on these continents adrift, steered by fickle winds. To look below, unto the world's surface, is to witness a seething hell. Few who visit that wasteland return; and those who do are cursed a painful death. ##And yet what do we truly know of the World Rend? Rumours, hearsay, legend. It is the most important historical event, yet it remains a mystery. The Emberians, whose civilisation reached its peak at the dawn of this terrible new age, stored all their wisdom in magical cipher. Their technology was made inert by the Rend, everything was lost. We know more about the kings and queens of the Middle Ages - thanks to their humble quills - than we do the Emberians. ##And so, in this age of ignorance, do I strive to collect what fragments of truth I can gleam. My own quill may yet prove a more powerful instrument than a century of Emberian technology. ##The World Rend occurred in the year 984. That we even still use the old calendar is a miracle of the Chronos Guild; for the slow-turning Neuron Star of Old Wikka, upon which the clocks of old were set, was destroyed in the event. ##Most accounts depict the Rend as a flash of magical energy. It engulfed the world, searing its surface and destroying every city and every settlement found below. Only those few people survived - outcast and adrift on the islands of the sky. ##Because the Emberians shunned the instability of the flying continents, few of their outposts existed here. In a pertinent irony, those who were outcast from Emberian civilisation - the Wikkans and the Endless, to name but two - suddenly outnumbered their old rivals. And thus the last remnants of Emberian civilisation were torn apart by their enemies. ##But from the ashes, new societies emerged. Survivors banded into groups and rebuilt as best they could. Emberian technology proved useless, so a new generation of humanity rekindled old knowledge. Houses were raised of brick and stone, magic spells were re-learned with simple cipher. The Wikkans and their gods found power anew, and their covens were built in every city. ##Now, as I write from the thriving realm of Byonne, I cannot help but smile at our accomplishments. But it is a smile tinged with sadness, for we still toil in the shadow of that terrible cataclysm. We still bear the trauma of the World Rend.
Chinese: 世界撕裂。尽管它早已隐入遥远的记忆,人们谈起它时仍会压低声音,惴惴不安。因为谁不仍畏惧那场把我们的城市夷平、把我们的智慧涤荡、把我们赶上天空的浩劫呢?##没有谁还记得脚下坚实的土地。一代代人生于死于这些漂荡的大陆,任凭无常的风摆布。俯瞰下方,望向世界地表,便是目睹一座沸腾的地狱。造访那片荒原的人鲜有生还;生还者也被诅咒以痛苦的死亡。##然而,关于世界撕裂,我们究竟知道什么?传闻,道听途说,传说。它是最重要的历史事件,却仍是一个谜。余烬人——他们的文明在这可怖新纪元的黎明达到顶峰——把全部智慧储存在魔法密文里。他们的科技在撕裂中失效,一切尽失。多亏中世纪帝王们谦逊的笔杆,我们对他们的了解,反而胜过对余烬人的了解。##于是,在这个蒙昧的时代,我努力搜集所能拾得的真相残片。我的笔杆,或许终将证明比一个世纪的余烬科技更有力。##世界撕裂发生于984年。我们至今仍在使用旧历,可谓时序公会的奇迹;因为旧时钟所校准的古维坎神经元星,在那场事件中毁灭了。##大多数记载把撕裂描绘成一道魔法能量的闪光。它吞没世界,灼烧地表,毁灭了下方每一座城市和聚落。只有寥寥数人幸存——被放逐、漂泊于天空的岛屿。##因为余烬人回避飞行大陆的不稳定,他们的前哨在此寥寥。颇具讽刺意味的是,那些被余烬文明放逐的人——维坎人和无尽者,仅举两例——转眼间在数量上压过了旧日对手。于是,余烬文明最后的残余被他们的敌人撕成了碎片。##但从灰烬中,新的社会崛起了。幸存者们结成群体,尽力重建。余烬科技被证明无用,新一代人类重新点燃了古老的知识。砖石垒起房屋,人们用简单的密文重新学会咒语。维坎人和他们的神重获力量,他们的女巫团建在了每座城中。##如今,当我在繁荣的拜昂写下这些,我不禁为我们的成就微笑。但那微笑带着一丝哀伤,因为我们仍在那场可怕浩劫的阴影下辛劳。我们仍背负着世界撕裂的创伤。

English: On Paeguth, by Theodore Hubert - 1389
Chinese: 论帕古斯,西奥多·休伯特著——1389

English: Paeguth. In ancient times, no speck of land in the bounds of the fallen empire had not felt the loving touch of their miasmic embrace. So ubiquitous was their presence that crumbling effigies can still be found to this day; though it is unlikely most would recognize them as such.##Like all early Gods, the shape Paeguth took upon their arrival bears little resemblance to how we picture them today. Early accounts depict Paeguth as a soft and gentle creature; half the stature of a normal person and with a bleating voice not unlike a baby lamb. Wherever Paeguth tread, life spilled forth. Whenever new life sprang up, Paeguth was sure to follow. So entwined werre they to life and growth that the Wikkans granted them governorship over these domains: the God of Fertility, life, and abundance.##As with all Gods, Paeguth changed with time. His change was not a gentle one. In the middle ages, when Elswyn initiated the War of Weeping, Paeguth joined those that sought to oppose her destructive tide. However, Paeguth soon found that life was more easily cut short than nurtured. They watched scores of their most beloved cut low by Elswyn's crimson axe. Each crumpled body scarred Paeguth's soul. And in that bed of scars, their heart hardened.##Paeguth retreated deep into a dark cave untouched by war. There they studied the hardy creatures that eked out a meagre existence in the darkest untouched corners of the earth. They learned that life can endure when one discards such foolish notions as beauty and grandeur. When Paeguth emerged, their grotesque body heralded in a new order: life unending, at any cost.##Many would recoil at the God's new terrifying visage. Many others would come to welcome their blissfully cancerous embrace. Those that worshipped them would slowly be warped into new grotesque forms. Though hideous, these creatures were engineered for almost limitless survival. ##It is unclear if Paeguth survived the World Rend. Many theorise that the earth's sundering was enough to finally shatter the once-loved God. Others believe - or perhaps pray - that they have once again returned to their cave, and will again bestow the gift of nigh everlasting life upon their faithful followers.
Chinese: 帕古斯。远古之时,堕落帝国疆域内没有一寸土地不曾感受过他们瘴气般拥抱的爱抚。他们的存在无处不在,以至于至今仍能找到残破的神像;尽管大多数人多半认不出那是什么。##和所有早期神明一样,帕古斯降临时所具的形貌,与我们今日想象的大相径庭。早期记载把帕古斯描绘成一种柔软温和的造物;身高只有常人一半,叫声咩咩,活像羊羔。帕古斯踏足之处,生命涌流。新生命萌发之地,帕古斯必然随后而至。他们与生命和生长如此紧密相连,维坎人便授予他们对这些领域的治理权:丰饶之神,生命与丰足之神。##和所有神明一样,帕古斯随时间改变了。他的改变并不温和。中世纪,当艾尔温挑起哭泣之战时,帕古斯加入了反抗她毁灭浪潮的行列。然而,帕古斯很快发现,扼杀生命远比养育生命容易。他们眼看着最心爱的生灵成片倒在艾尔温的猩红之斧下。每一具蜷曲的尸体都在帕古斯的灵魂上留下伤疤。在那片伤疤之上,他们的心变硬了。##帕古斯退入一座未受战火波及的黑暗洞穴深处。在那里,他们研究那些在地球最黑暗、最偏远的角落里勉强求生的坚韧生物。他们悟到,只要抛弃美与宏伟这类愚蠢的观念,生命便能延续。当帕古斯再度现身,他们怪诞的身躯昭示了一种新秩序:不计一切代价的、无终结的生命。##许多人在这位神明新添的可怖面容前退缩。另许多人则开始欢迎他们那幸福得如癌症般的拥抱。崇拜他们的人会慢慢被扭曲成新的怪诞形态。虽然丑陋,这些造物却被塑造成近乎无限的生存机器。##帕古斯是否在世界撕裂中幸存,不得而知。许多人推断,大地崩裂足以最终粉碎这位曾受爱戴的神。另一些人相信——或者说祈愿——他们再次回到了自己的洞穴,并将再一次把近乎永恒的生命馈赠给忠诚的信徒。

English: CALLING ALL DENIZENS OF THE APOSTATIC UNION!
Chinese: 叛教联盟全体居民注意!

English: Our land is beset with a most terrible famine. Can you sit idle while your crops fail and your loved ones perish? ## We all know who is to blame - The god worshipper! The cultist! For too long they have uttered their dread prayers from the fringes of society, bringing terrible omens upon our lands. ## Our Polymath humbly requests the aid of every denizen in this matter. Visit the Apostatic Union's Council building, in the centre of town, to enquire further.
Chinese: 我们的土地正被一场可怕的饥荒折磨。当你的庄稼歉收、亲人死去时,你能坐视不管吗?##我们都知道该怪谁——神明崇拜者!邪教徒!太久以来,他们一直在社会的边缘念诵可怖的祷词,给我们的土地招来凶兆。##我们的博学家谦恭地请求每一位居民在此事上出力。请前往镇中心的叛教联盟议事厅进一步咨询。

English: The Hidden Truth of Cipher, by Anonymous
Chinese: 密文的隐秘真相,佚名著

English: The art of cipher magic is practised in every corner of the Apostatic Union, based on the learnings of its universities - yet there is a paradox at the very heart of their scripture. To speak openly about it will see the full wrath of the inquisition fall upon one's liberty, and so - for fear of rotting in some dark cell - I must hide the authorship of this treasie. But let it be known, I am a scholar of some renown.##It is entirely true that there is a hidden language to the cosmos. A series of symbols that comprise an incomplete alphabet known as cipher. Individually these symbols are meaningless; but when strung together into lines, they can have profound effects. This is the basis of all magic.##But while human scribes must painstakingly etch out each symbol, their pens heavy with the import of the task - the gods' very thoughts are writ in cipher and magic comes to them easily.##Nonetheless, the gods are still bound to the rules of cipher. This was the philosophical justification for the God War, the renunciation of Wikkan control - and the forming of the Apostatic Union. For if humans and gods draw from the same power, the argument went, then why must we submit ourselves to a divine hierarchy?##Indeed, the first Union polymath theorised that cipher itself was created by humanity; that in the cave-dwelling days of prehistory, humans discovered a power in themselves and built a language around this power, that etched itself upon the cosmos. As human superstition led them to pray to divine beings of their imagination, such beings were made manifest from that belief.##Such is the reasoning that lies at the very heart of the Apostatic Union - that man predated cipher, and to defy this supposed truth is to commit an act of treason in the Union.##But in the past few decades, scholars have made incredible advances in cipher research. We can study the cosmos with a precision not enjoyed since before the World Rend. And what have we discovered? That there are certain rules written into the very fabric of existence. A sentence - theoretical, but very likely to exist - threads itself through this world, and every world.##This sentence explains the limitations of our spells. Why we cannot reverse the flow of time; why we cannot resurrect the long-dead. But most important of all, it was written long before humans existed, and it is written in cipher.##By whom? We cannot say - and likely never will, because the Inquisition has taken every  possible step to repress this research. I have witnessed my contempoaries disappear; others threatened into silence. I have watched entire library wings burned down to the ground.##But it is imperative that we spread the truth. An ideology founded upon a lie is rotten to the core.
Chinese: 密文魔法之术盛行于叛教联盟的每个角落,以各大学府的学说为基础——然而在他们的经文正中心,存在一个悖论。公开谈论它,宗教裁判所的全部怒火就会落到你的自由头上;因此——唯恐在某间黑牢里烂掉——我必须隐去这篇论文的作者身份。但要知道,我是小有名气的学者。##宇宙存在一种隐秘语言,这千真万确。一系列符号构成一部不完整的字母表,人称密文。单独来看,这些符号毫无意义;但当它们连缀成行,便能产生深远的影响。这是一切魔法的基础。##人类的誊写师必须苦心刻写每一个符号,笔尖因使命之重而沉坠——而神的思想本身就是密文写就,魔法于他们轻而易举。##尽管如此,神明仍受密文规则的束缚。这正是神之战的哲学依据:摒弃维坎的控制,建立叛教联盟。因为若人类与神明汲取同一种力量,论点如此,那我们为何要臣服于神圣的等级制度?##事实上,联盟的第一位博学家曾推论,密文本身是人类的造物;在穴居的史前时代,人类在自身中发现了一种力量,并围绕这种力量构建了一门语言,这门语言镌刻在了宇宙之上。随着人类的迷信引导他们向自己想象出的神圣存在祈祷,这样的存在便从那信仰中显形。##这就是叛教联盟最核心的信条:人类先于密文,否认这一所谓的真理,在联盟便是叛国。##但在过去几十年,学者们在密文研究上取得了惊人的进展。我们可以用世界撕裂之前都不曾有过的精度研究宇宙。我们发现了什么?存在某些规则,写进了存在的织体本身。一个句子——理论上的,但极有可能存在——贯穿这个世界,贯穿每一个世界。##这个句子解释了我们法术的局限。为何我们无法逆转时间之流;为何我们无法复活死去已久的人。但最重要的是,它的书写远早于人类存在,而且它是用密文写成的。##出自谁手?我们无从得知——多半永远不会知道,因为宗教裁判所已采取一切可能的手段压制这项研究。我目睹我的同侪接连消失;另一些人被威胁闭嘴。我眼看着整座整座的图书馆翼楼被烧成白地。##但我们必须传播真相。建立在谎言之上的意识形态,从根上就是烂的。

English: A Guide to the Oneiric Isles, by Niccolo Lopo - 1442
Chinese: 梦幻群岛指南,尼科洛·洛波著——1442

English: It was a sweltering day in Riova when my editor burst through the door. The twin stars of Vena were dancing high that day, bathing the city in a searing yellow haze.##"Niccolo!" he yelled, after nearly dislodging my front door from its hinges. The impact of his entry had caused my house to sway, suspended as it was - like all houses in Riova - from the interconnected web of pulleys, cables and bridges that kept the city aloft.##"You are going to the Oneiric Isles!" he declared. "Your ship leaves tomorrow."##I must confess, I was taken aback. The periodical I wrote for - The Weekly Wail - was mostly concerned with the petty dramas of Riova's wealthy elite, with little penchant for travel memoir. But then, the proliferation of cipher-based periodicals, with their self-updating calligraphy, was making my editor nervous. He had clearly decided that sending me to the arse-end of nowhere, to my certain demise, would titillate our readership and bring in some coin. ##Many citizens know of the Oneiric Isles only from fairy tales. It is a small archipelago of little political import, drifting around the southernmost edge of the Apostatic Union's borders. While its central region of Hallowshire saw fierce fighting during the God War, it has only recently been absorbed into the Apostatic Union's territorial sphere. ##What both excited my editor - and perturbed myself - was the inarguable wildness of these strange islands. They are illuminated by a single neuron star, which orbits close to the islands, dousing them in a magenta light. ##The Wikkan Coven of the Worm has long squirmed in the dark recesses of Hallowshire, and has caused nothing but trouble for the Union forces stationed there. Similarly, the historic lawlessness of that place has made it a dark haven for smugglers, pirates and brigands alike. ##Meanwhile, beyond the Union's territory lies even stranger islands. The archipelago's western edges are home to the notorious Endless; who feature in many whispered old-wive's tales, but have rarely been glimpsed by mortal eyes. ##The eastern islands, mind you, are very different. The realm of Kardova, which famously declined to enter the Apostatic Union's commonwealth after the God War, has been found there. Its exact relocation cannot be dated, as is so often the case with islands drifting unrecorded through the skyrealms - but the strange, complex machines that are being constructed there have caught the attention of many of the Union's scholars and aetherists. ##To travel to such a place, then, was a folly of the highest order. Indeed, I would have turned down the venture in an instant - were I not facing imminent bankruptcy. So with a heavy heart, I accepted and began to pack my things. ##These volumes, originally published in my column in The Weekly Wail, recount my foolhardy venture into the strange and dangerous Oneiric Isles.
Chinese: 那是个里奥瓦闷热的日子,我的编辑撞门而入。那天维纳的双子星在高空起舞,把整座城浸在灼热的黄色雾霭里。##"尼科洛!"他吼道,差点把我的前门从铰链上撞下来。他闯入的冲力让我的房子摇摇晃晃——它和里奥瓦所有房屋一样,悬吊在让整座城凌空而立的滑轮、缆索与桥梁相互勾连的大网上。##"你要去梦幻群岛!"他宣布。"你的船明天出发。"##我必须承认,我吃了一惊。我供职的刊物——《每周哀号》——主要关注里奥瓦豪门富贵的鸡毛蒜皮,对游记没什么兴趣。不过,密文刊物的激增,它们那会自我更新的书法,让我的编辑坐立不安。他显然已经打定主意:把我送到鸟不拉屎的穷乡僻壤去送死,既能吊起读者的胃口,又能赚点硬币。##许多公民对梦幻群岛的了解仅限于童话。它是一片无足轻重的小群岛,漂荡在叛教联盟边界的最南端。虽然它的中心区域哈洛郡在神之战中经历过激战,但它直到最近才被纳入联盟的领土范围。##让我的编辑兴奋——也让我自己不安的——是这些怪岛无可争辩的荒蛮。它们由一颗神经元星照亮,这颗星紧贴群岛运转,把它们泡在洋红色的光里。##蠕虫女巫团长年在哈洛郡幽暗的角落里蠕动,给驻扎此地的联盟部队惹尽了麻烦。同样,那地方史上无法无天,使它成了走私犯、海盗和劫匪共有的黑暗避风港。##与此同时,联盟疆界之外还有更古怪的岛屿。群岛西部边缘是臭名昭著的无尽者的家园;他们在许多窃窃私语的老太婆故事里出场,却难得被凡人亲眼得见。##不过,东边的岛屿就截然不同了。神之战后拒不加入联盟联邦的卡尔多瓦,竟在那里被人发现。它确切的重定位置无法断代——在天空领域无人记录漂流的岛屿向来如此——但那里正在建造的奇异复杂的机器,已经引起联盟许多学者和乙太师的注意。##要去那样的地方,简直是愚不可及。说实话,若不是濒临破产,我立刻就会回绝这趟差事。于是我怀着沉重的心情接受了,开始收拾行装。##这几卷文字最初刊于我在《每周哀号》的专栏,记述了我闯入奇异而危险的梦幻群岛的莽撞之行。

English: Recollections from the God War, by Juliana Liddell - 1412
Chinese: 神战回忆录,朱莉安娜·利德尔著——1412

English: Before our airship rose a writhing mass of flesh. Taller than any tree, any structure, any living thing; it filled the horizon with its ghastly form. A hand rose to thwart us - or should I say, many hands - for the thing's flesh bubbled and boiled with minute approximations of the whole. Its arm was made from many arms. Its screaming face had countless gaping mouths. ##The captain's voice bellowed across the deck. Being no navy woman, I cannot recount these orders, but the ship began to lurch to the side - a futile attempt at evasion. ##With an almighty crash I was flung against the ship's bow. We spun in freefall. Through splinters and dust I could see the other half of the ship; we had been split in twain and the ground was rushing to meet us. ##The ship exploded into fragments as it struck land, but I did not feel the impact. I levitated just inches from the wreckage, a glow encircling me. I could see the hand of an Erudite Academy scholar buried in the rubble - it twitched, the glow flickered, and I fell safely to the ground. I know not who saved my life in place of their own - but I think of them often.##The creature towered above me, staring with many eyes; howling with many mouths. These were the closing months of the God War, and the Wikkans had become desperate. Faced with their annihilation, they had embraced practices that had long been forbidden. Whatever lurched towards me had once been a god - though it could not be called that any more. ##As it raised its arms to strike me, its bulk blocked the light of the neuron star. Against my better judgement, against the very ideology to which I had committed myself, I uttered a prayer to my family's patron god. A god I had seen cut to pieces not a month before. ##Who knows - maybe some vestigial remnant of that god yet remained, and took pity on me?##A hideous noise erupted from the monster. Its flesh had always shifted in some eldritch pattern, but now it appeared to flow like liquid. Huge chunks of it began to drop to the ground, exposing glimpses of a skeleton. Whatever spell the Wikkans had cast, whatever power flowed through this entity - it was failing.##At that moment, our sister ship burst from the clouds at blistering speed. A dozen cannons erupted into fire and the creature rippled with explosions. A voidstone lance - itself the size of a small vessel - was flung directly into the monster's skull. ##The thing buckled and bent under its own weight. It appeared to be melting. The skin tore around its neck, and its head bent back in an unnatural way - eventually dropping to the ground (I would later discover that it crushed a nearby pub). After a few moments all appeared to be left was a steaming mound of flesh and bone.
Chinese: 在我们的飞艇前方,耸立着一团蠕动的血肉。比任何树、任何建筑、任何生物都高;它可怖的身躯遮满了地平线。一只手扬起阻挡我们——或者说,是许多只手——因为那东西的血肉里咕嘟翻滚着无数整体的缩影。它的手臂由许多手臂构成。它嘶吼的脸上有数不清的裂开的大嘴。##船长的声音在甲板上轰鸣。我不是海军出身,无法复述那些口令,但飞船开始向侧面猛倾——一次徒劳的闪避。##一声巨响,我被甩向船头。我们在自由落体中打转。透过木屑与尘土,我能看见飞船的另一半;我们被劈成了两半,地面正迎面扑来。##飞船撞地时炸成碎片,但我没有感到冲击。我悬浮在离残骸几寸的地方,一圈光晕环绕着我。我能看见一位博识学院学者的手埋在瓦砾中——它抽搐了一下,光晕闪烁,我便安然落地。我不知是谁用自己的性命换回了我的——但我常常想起他们。##那造物在我头顶耸立,用许多眼睛凝视;用许多嘴嚎叫。那是神之战的最后几个月,维坎人已经绝望。面对灭顶之灾,他们拥抱了久已被禁止的行径。朝我扑来的那东西曾是一位神——虽然已不能再这么称呼它。##当它举臂要击打我时,它庞大的身躯挡住了神经元星的光。违背我的理智,违背我毕生信奉的信条,我向家守护神念出了一句祈祷。一位不到一个月前,我亲眼看着被碎尸万段的神。##谁知道呢——也许那神尚存一缕残魂,垂怜于我?##一声骇人的巨响从怪物体内爆出。它的血肉原本就以一种诡异的模式蠕动,此刻却像液体一样流淌开来。大块大块的血肉开始坠向地面,露出一截骨架的端倪。无论维坎人施了什么咒,无论什么力量在这造物中流淌——它正在失效。##就在那时,我们的姊妹船以灼热的速度冲破云层。十几门加农炮喷出烈火,怪物的身躯在爆炸中震颤。一支虚空石长矛——本身有一艘小船那么大——被径直掷入怪物的头颅。##那东西在自己的重量下弯折、塌陷。它似乎在融化。它颈部的皮肤撕裂开来,它的头以一种不自然的方式向后弯去——最终坠落在地(我后来得知,它压塌了附近一家酒馆)。片刻之后,剩下的似乎只有一堆冒着热气的血肉与骨头。

English: A Foolhardy Voyage, by Stultus Navigatio - 1426
Chinese: 莽夫之航,斯图尔图斯·纳维加提奥著——1426

English: As I write this account, my quill wavers in my hand. I can see the skin peeling and flaking from my fingers; blood and pus seeping from the cracks. Before the sepsis sets in, I hope to recount my fateful voyage to the Emberian city of Nodlem. It was my final voyage, and these will be my final words.##The expedition was funded by the Erudite Academy. They had us sign numerous documents and waivers, no doubt written from the safety of some Riovan legal office, clearing them of any accountability. I was not perturbed; I thought our success was assured.##The vessel we travelled in was outfitted with the latest in cipher-technology. We had hired an aetherist, who hermetically sealed the thing with numerous cipher-wards and provided us with the finely crafted garments that allows one to survive in the outer-reaches of the cosmos. But when I asked the aetherist to accompany us (for a healthy salary, no less), he replied:##'The underlands? Nay. I have flown into the cosmos on six occasions, and stared into its inky blackness. I have delved into the dread depths of Slev's poison lake, and escaped unscathed. I have been to unspeakable places, but the underlands? I will not go there.'##We anchored our galleon in the southernmost skies of the Apostatic Union, close to the near-lawless archipelago of the Oneiric Isles. The galleon's captain was wary of pirates, but I insisted we would be back before the nearby neuron star withdrew its reddish glare.##Our shuttle detached itself from the galleon, shaking as we made our descent through the clouds. My crew sat uneasy as the light faded. In the four hundred years since the World Rend, few have visited the world's surface and lived to recount it.##But our landing was uneventful enough. We opened the hatch to find the glistening bones of a city stretching towards the sky. Huge metal structures arched overhead, supported by girders of an impossible scale, that no living blacksmith could reproduce. ##We set to work examining the ruins. Legend describes how the Emberians wrote nothing with ink; they stored their knowledge in vast networks of cipher, accessible to any citizen, so that each and every person was as learned as a great scholar or polymath. Lamentably, this proved to be true - for we could find no book, no page, no scrap of writing to shed light on the mystery of their culture. ##What we found were towering halls, once used for some inscrutable bureaucratic purpose but which now lay overtaken by fungi. We saw evidence of the rail-ships that hauled cargo of unimaginable weight, and the great portal-relays that are said to have connected every corner of the world. ##We stared, bewildered, through the eye-goggles of our protective hoods. My faith in the wonders of aetherist technology was well founded; the accursed earth could not infect us with its taint. So long as our suits remained intact, we were safe -but there was just one factor I had not accounted for.##The scream echoed through the halls. We spun to see one of our crew collapsed on the floor; blood gurgling from his suit. As we made our way to investigate, I caught something in my periphery - too quick to see - and I turned to see another of us standing plainly with no head upon her shoulders. She crumpled into the darkness without making a sound.##So, we ran. ##The suits were cumbersome and the air thick with spores. I cannot say how the other crew met their fate; I heard cries, but did not falter in my flight. In my arrogance I had assumed tales of monsters were but fictions of dying men; for what could survive down here in this wasteland? But as I neared the shuttle, exhausted and terrified, one of the creatures appeared plainly before me.##I have heard tales of ghosts, but this was not one. It was a shadow incarnate; a swirling amorphous presence. A spectral arm emerged from that dread mass, which became a scythe as it swung towards me. I ducked and sprinted to the shuttle, narrowly escaping its ephemeral blade. As I closed the shuttle's hatch I could see the creature in chase, and I swear I saw a face there - staring at me not with rage or malice, but with a terrible sadness in its eyes.##When I returned to the safety of the skyrealms, it became clear that the creature had torn a large gash in my protective suit. Over the coming days I became rapt with terrible agony as my skin blackened and split. I exist now, a week since our voyage, in a state of prolonged decay - my consciousness being the last remnant of humanity left in this revolting husk of a body. It will not be long until I succumb fully to the Death Veil curse. ##Let this be a warning to those who wish to follow in my footsteps. The Emberian civilisation, which ruled every corner of the world some four-hundred years ago, is forever lost - and to go in search of its secrets is to meet a terrible fate.
Chinese: 写这篇记述时,我的羽毛笔在手中颤抖。我能看见我手指上的皮肤剥落、成片掉下;血与脓从裂口中渗出。在败血症发作之前,我想记述我那趟注定要命的远航,去往余烬城市诺德勒姆。那是我最后一次远航,这些也将是我最后的文字。##远征由博识学院资助。他们让我们签了无数文件和免责书,无疑是在里奥瓦某间安稳的法务办公室里写就的,好撇清他们的一切责任。我不以为意;我以为成功是板上钉钉的。##我们乘坐的飞行器装备了最先进的密文科技。我们雇了一位乙太师,他用无数密文护符把船封得密不透风,还为我们提供了能在宇宙外域存活的精工细作的衣服。可当我请乙太师同行(待遇可不薄),他答道:##'地下之地?不去。我六次飞入过宇宙,凝视过它漆黑的深渊。我下过斯列夫毒湖的可怖深处,毫发无伤地脱身。我去过难以言说的地方,但地下之地?我不去。'##我们把大帆船泊在联盟最南端的天域,紧邻几乎无法无天的梦幻群岛。大帆船船长对海盗心存戒备,但我坚持我们会在附近神经元星收起红光之前回来。##我们的穿梭艇脱离大帆船,在穿云而下时颠簸不已。光线渐暗,我的船员们坐立难安。自世界撕裂以来的四百年间,到过世界地表还能活着讲述的人寥寥无几。##不过我们的着陆总算平安无事。我们打开舱门,看见一座城市的莹莹白骨伸向天空。巨大的金属结构在头顶拱起,由规模超乎想象的构架支撑,任何在世的铁匠都复制不出。##我们着手考察废墟。传说余烬人不用墨水书写;他们把知识储存在庞大的密文网络中,任何公民皆可取用,因此每一个人都像大学者或博学家一样有学问。可叹,此言不虚——因为我们找不到一本书、一页纸、一片字,能揭示他们文化的奥秘。##我们看到的是高耸的厅堂,曾经用于某种不可理喻的官僚事务,如今已被真菌侵占。我们看到了轨道船的痕迹,它们曾拖运难以想象的重物;还有那些巨大的传送门中继,据说曾连通世界的每个角落。##我们隔着防护头罩的护目镜,茫然凝视。我对乙太科技奇观的信任是有根据的;受诅咒的大地无法感染我们。只要防护服完好无损,我们就安全——只是有一个因素我没有料到。##一声尖叫在大厅中回荡。我们转身,看见一名船员倒在地上;血从他的防护服里汩汩涌出。我们赶去查看时,余光里掠过什么东西——快得看不清——我回头,看见另一个同伴直挺挺地站着,肩上已没有头。她无声地倒进黑暗里。##于是,我们逃了。##防护服笨重,空气里满是孢子。我说不出其他船员遭遇了什么;我听见喊叫,却没有在奔逃中有半分迟疑。狂妄如我,原以为怪物的传说不过是垂死之人的杜撰;在这片荒原上,什么东西能活下来?可当我精疲力竭、魂飞魄散地接近穿梭艇时,一只造物清清楚楚地出现在我面前。##我听过幽灵的故事,但这不是幽灵。它是成形的暗影;一团旋绕的无定形存在。一条幽灵般的手臂从那可怖的团块中伸出,挥向我时化作一柄镰刀。我一低头冲向穿梭艇,险险躲过它虚渺的刃。在我关上舱门时,我能看见那造物追来,我发誓我看见了一张脸——它注视我的眼神里没有愤怒或恶意,只有一种可怖的悲伤。##当我回到天空领域的安全之地,事情已很清楚:那造物在我的防护服上撕开了一道大口子。此后几天,我的皮肤发黑、开裂,我被可怕的痛楚攫住。如今,距我们远航已过去一周,我处在漫长的腐烂之中——我的意识,是这具可憎躯壳里所剩的最后一点人性。用不了多久,我就会彻底屈服于死亡之幕的诅咒。##愿以此文警醒那些想步我后尘的人。四百年前统治世界每个角落的余烬文明,已永远失落——追寻它的秘密,就是迎向可怕的命运。

English: Cadish Rakehill Volume 1, by John Phlegming
Chinese: 卡迪什·雷克希尔 第一卷,约翰·弗莱明著

English: Cadish Rakehill awoke to a cornucopia of pain. His joints ached, his eyes stung and his head felt as if it had been dragged down a flight of stairs. He felt his lip; swollen and bloody. He checked his purse; completely empty. He probably should have been alarmed, but Cadish was worryingly acclimatised to waking in such a state. Except for being in the branches of a giant tree - this was new. ##And it was, indeed, a very large tree. Its trunk, enormous in girth, was home to numerous dwellings; houses that clung to its bark like insects. He glanced downwards and saw nothing but clouds; and when he looked up, a crooked castle rose above a mountain of leaves. ##Ah, a castle on top of a tree. Now he remembered. He was in the forest city of Kruve, in the northern reaches of Lundel. The only place crazy enough to build a castle on top of a fucking tree. ##He remembered getting very drunk in a gambling den in Rorke, and losing a lot of money to some scoundrel who claimed to be a princess. He had bet a considerable sum on the notion that she was definitely not a princess; and, to prove him wrong, she had taken him in an avian taxi to Kruve. He must have fallen asleep in the bird's back-mounted cabin, for the next thing he knew, he was in the stone walls of a rather dingy castle.##It turned out that the scoundrel was, in fact, a princess - and she wanted Cadish to pay up. He refused on the grounds that, being in such a decrepit castle, she can't have been a very good princess. The last thing he remembered was a princess punching him in the face. ##He looked down the branch. A couple of well-armed guards blocked the exit - ah, so this branch was, in fact, a prison. He had to admit, it was one of the more pleasant prisons he had found himself in.##He sat nursing his head for some time. The blue neuron star of Lundel was distant here; it kept the tree in a greyish half-light. This was unlikely to change anytime soon, seeing as the sluggish orbit of Lundel's star made a single day as long as a Riovan month. Most citizens would toil in labour for much of the long-day, and get drunk in equal measure for most of the long-night. Cadish, of course, got drunk during both. ##Suddenly, he realised a figure was standing in front of him. He had not noticed her appear, and yet it felt as though she had been there a long time. She was clothed in a sari of brilliant red -  a garment from the distant island of Puria - and a veil of glinting gold obscured all but her eyes.##"Cadish Rakehill, I presume?"##Cadish sat there - dumbfounded - for a good few moments until he remembered to nod. ##Her eyes creased into a smile. "I have heard much of your adventures, Cadish. You are said to have acquired a treasure from every corner of the skyrealms in your time as a mercenary." ##He nodded again, not mentioning that he had lost just as many treasures in various gambling halls of disrepute.##"I have a job for you, Cadish. Do you remember the pirate captain Jinesh?"##He swallowed. He remembered Jinesh. He remembered the man's contemptible grin. He remembered the man's gleaming sabre, held against his neck. ##"Jinesh wants to meet with you. I can make this happen." ##Cadish frowned. "You said this was a job. So, what's the pay?"##The woman drew a serpent-like creature from her sari. Its segmented body was like that of a giant, glistening maggot - but its head was full of rows upon rows of sharp teeth. It was a vampiric parasite. ##"The payment is your life", she said, as she flung the creature towards him.##Before he could move, it whipped itself around him and its head forced itself into his mouth. Its slimy body lurched down his throat, shifting and wriggling, until it was completely inside him. His stomach writhed as he retched to no avail. ##"Don't worry Cadish Rakehill," she said. "It will all be over soon."##She snapped her fingers and, just like that, he fell into a dark stupor. ##
Chinese: 卡迪什·雷克希尔在疼痛的大合唱中醒来。他关节酸痛,眼睛刺痛,脑袋像是被拖着下了一整段楼梯。他摸摸嘴唇;肿胀带血。他摸摸钱袋;空空如也。他本该惊慌,但卡迪什对这种状态醒来早已熟练得令人担忧。除了——身处一棵巨树的枝杈之间,这是新鲜事。##而那确实是棵非常大的树。它的树干粗大无比,上面住着无数居所;一座座房子像昆虫一样扒在树皮上。他往下看,只见云海;往上看,一座歪歪扭扭的城堡耸立在树叶堆成的山上。##啊,树顶上的城堡。他记起来了。他在伦德尔北部的森林之城克鲁夫。全天下唯一疯到会把城堡盖在一颗该死的树顶上的地方。##他想起自己在罗克的赌场喝得烂醉,输了一大笔钱给一个自称公主的骗子。他押了一大笔赌她绝对不是公主;而为了证明他错了,她带上他乘鸟出租车来了克鲁夫。他准是在鸟背上的舱室里睡着了,因为他回过神来时,已经在一座相当寒酸的城堡石墙里了。##原来那骗子确实是位公主——而她要卡迪什付账。他拒绝的理由是,住在这么破的城堡里,她八成不是什么好公主。他记得的最后一幕,是公主一拳打在他脸上。##他顺着树枝望下去。两个全副武装的卫兵堵住出口——啊,原来这根树枝其实是座牢房。不得不承认,这是他蹲过的高级牢房之一。##他坐着揉了半天脑袋。伦德尔的蓝色神经元星在这里很遥远;它让树城浸在灰蒙蒙的半光里。这种情形短期内不会变,因为伦德尔之星迟缓的轨道使一个白昼有里奥瓦一个月那么长。大多数市民在漫长白昼里做工,又在漫长黑夜里对等买醉。卡迪什嘛,自然是两段都醉。##忽然,他发觉一个人影站在面前。他没有察觉她何时出现,却感觉她似乎已在那里很久。她身披艳红的纱丽——来自遥远的普利亚岛的服饰——一层闪光的金纱遮住了她的一切,只露出一双眼睛。##"卡迪什·雷克希尔,我猜?"##卡迪什呆坐在那里,好半天才想起要点头。##她眼角弯成笑意。"卡迪什,你的冒险我听过许多。据说你做雇佣兵的时候,天空领域每个角落的宝贝都收过一件。"##他又点头,没提他在各路下三滥赌场里也输掉了同样多的宝贝。##"我有一单活给你,卡迪什。还记得海盗船长吉内什吗?"##他咽了口唾沫。他记得吉内什。记得那家伙可鄙的狞笑。记得那把闪亮的军刀抵在自己脖子上。##"吉内什想见你。我能安排。"##卡迪什皱眉。"你说这是一单活。那报酬是什么?"##那女人从纱丽里抽出一条蛇状的生物。它的分节身体像一条巨大的、油亮的蛆——脑袋里却长满一排排利齿。那是一只吸血寄生虫。##"报酬是你的命",她说着,把那生物朝他掷来。##他还没来得及动,那东西已甩身缠上他,头颅直钻进他的嘴里。它黏滑的身体顺着他的喉咙蠕动而下,扭动着、拱动着,直到完全没入他体内。他干呕不止,胃里翻江倒海。##"别担心,卡迪什·雷克希尔,"她说。"很快就都结束了。"##她打了个响指,他就此坠入昏黑的迷惘。##

English: On Remembrance, by Chirrius - 1278
Chinese: 论追忆，克里乌斯 著 - 1278 年

English: When I was just ten and two years of age, while exploring in the forests of Verdant, my brother and I stumbled upon a clearing full of fleeting starlights - that long extinct flower that bloomed just once a year. ##My brother stood smiling amid those flowers. In one smooth motion they rippled around him, each unfurling their petals in some ancient rhythm. Tiny droplets, emitting a pale white light, drifted upwards like frozen tears. For a moment the whole forest seemed to be full of them; glittering in union, reflected in my brother's eyes.##But this memory, like so many others, is little more than a dream. I can recount colourful prose, but further details escape me. What was the colour of my brother's hair? What did his face really look like? What was his name? ##For all of us endless, Verdant exists in this dream-state. We fill our memoirs with elegant prose but we argue over the details. It has been hundreds of years since our lungs could swell with that sweet air, and between then and now - between Verdant and the Realm of the Endless - there is trauma that stains our minds like spilled ink. ##I can recall another memory of my brother. I see his face, covered in blood. I see his mouth, locked in a silent scream. I see raging fires reflected in his eyes. For that was the day I devoured his still-living body.##If Verdant is our dream, the Years of Devouring are our nightmare. Though we stage plays and write novels of what happened then, few speak of our personal guilt. That hunger, that rage, that blood mist; the remembrance comes to us in pangs of sorrow. ##But there are yet others who deny its tragedy. Who justify their hunger and their deeds with flimsy arguments. Those who would revive the Cadaver Crusades, and see us feast upon flesh once more. Those who have allowed themselves to forget. ##So reader, I beseech you; do not languish in the sweetness of your dreams if you are not willing to recall the horrors of your nightmares. We all carry a burden of guilt. To deny it is to relinquish the last shred of our humanity - and then we are truly lost.
Chinese: 十二岁那年，我和哥哥在苍翠森林里探险时，撞见了一片开满转瞬星光的空地——那种一年只开一次、如今早已灭绝的花。##哥哥站在花丛中央微笑着。花瓣以某种古老的节律在他周围层层绽放。细小的水珠泛着苍白的微光，如凝固的泪滴般向上飘去。那一刻，整片森林似乎都充满了它们；交相辉映，倒映在哥哥的眼中。##但这段记忆，正如其他许多记忆一样，不过是一场梦。我能复述华美的辞章，细节却从指间溜走。哥哥的头发是什么颜色？他的脸究竟长什么样？他叫什么名字？##对我们所有无尽者而言，苍翠只存在于这种梦境状态中。我们在回忆录里堆砌优雅的散文，却又为细节争论不休。自我们的肺叶最后一次胀满那甜美的空气，已过去数百年——而在那时与此刻之间，在苍翠与无尽领域之间，创伤如泼洒的墨渍染污着我们的心灵。##我还记得哥哥的另一段记忆。我看见他的脸，沾满鲜血。我看见他的嘴，凝固在无声的尖叫中。我看见熊熊烈火映在他的眼中。因为那一天，我吞食了他尚有余温的躯体。##如果苍翠是我们的梦，吞噬之年便是我们的噩梦。虽然我们排演戏剧、撰写小说来记述那段过往，却少有人谈及自己内心的罪疚。那种饥饿，那种狂怒，那片血雾；追忆总伴着阵阵悲痛向我们袭来。##然而还有一些人否认那场悲剧。他们用站不住脚的诡辩为自己的饥饿与行径开脱。那些人想重启尸骸十字军，让我们再度以血肉为盛宴。那些人任由自己遗忘。##所以读者啊，我恳求你；倘若你不愿回忆噩梦中的恐怖，就不要沉溺于梦的甜美。我们每个人都背负着罪疚。否认它，便是交出我们仅存的人性——到那时，我们才真正迷失。

English: Buried Guilt, by Vleklum - 1156
Chinese: 深埋的罪，弗莱克鲁姆 著 - 1156 年

English: Ethur spurred the gelatinous flank of his steed, but to no avail. The creature still floated at the same sluggish pace, its tentacles trailing through the grass. He had no idea where Lord Arded had found such a creature, but it was little better than a silkslug. ##It swayed at an erratic pace that made Ethur's armour shift and chafe against his ancient skin. His body was always wracked with an assortment of pains and aches - such was the fate of being endless - but this constant irritation caused chunks of his flesh to come away when he itched. Flesh that would never grow back. ##As Ethur crossed a waybridge he glanced below. Miles downward, past floating islands and drifting clouds, he saw clusters of artificial lights - throbbing and pulsing in the gloom of the world's surface. For this story, dear reader, takes place in the first Cadaver Crusade, when Emberian cities still thrived.##Ethur's steed had stopped. He looked up to see a humble dwelling, not a few decades old. Smoke rose from its chimney, betraying its mortal inhabitants. Lord Arded would be pleased. ##He dismounted and drew his sword. Though his stomach growled, he would not feed today. Fresh meat was to be procured and returned to the war party; rations were then distributed fairly. That said, Ethur had long suspected that his Lord liked to keep his troops hungry, to cloud their judgement and foster their rage. ##The door buckled behind his weight easy enough. A boy stood before him, bewildered. Ethur's sword slid gently between the boy's ribs and he crumpled to the floor. Somewhere, a woman screamed; a familiar sound of late.##An old man burst forth and impaled Ethur with a spear. This was somewhat irritating, as his chest was already so full of holes that it whistled in strong winds. Ether grabbed the man by the throat and raised his sword to strike. ##But something stopped Ethur. As he looked at the man, he felt a stirring inside him. Something about those eyes; it was like looking into a cloudy mirror. Could it be?##The old man had stopped struggling against Ethur's grip, for the same distant recollection had dawned upon him as well. ##The old man swallowed, stuttered, then croaked: 'Father?'##Ethur's grip relaxed. He dropped the man, he dropped his sword. A horror engulfed him; the first glimmer of true emotion he had felt in a long time. ##Before he knew what was happening, a woman had picked up his sword and chopped off his head. The world rushed to meet him with a thud. He lay there, blinking slowly, as his family hacked his body into pieces. ##They buried Ethur in the garden, in a gesture of undeserved respect. He kept his face motionless, so they thought him truly dead; he was too cowardly to do otherwise. ##It was a shallow grave and sounds of the forest filtered down to him. When the guilt and shame subsided, he felt a kind of peace; being so close to those he once loved. Family. Son. He mouthed the words in the dirt, to an audience of worms and insects. ##But one day (or night, he knew not), he awoke from his mindless stupor to the sound of flames and screams. He listened to the cries, the carnage, the terror; but the silence that followed was worse. ##Then, voices; movement; a dazzling light. He was pulled from the dirt by his hair, held aloft by the grip of Lord Arded himself. The bastard's grin was a gash that spread from ear to ear.##'Well well", he said. "What've we found 'ere?'##Ethur looked past his Lord, to the smouldering house in the distance. Three fresh corpses were lined neatly in a row. ##
Chinese: 埃瑟尔夹了夹坐骑那凝胶般的侧腹，却无济于事。那生物仍以同样迟缓的速度漂浮着，触须拖过草丛。他完全不知道阿尔德勋爵是从哪儿找到这种生物的，但它比丝蛞蝓好不到哪儿去。##它摇摇晃晃，节奏紊乱，震得埃瑟尔的铠甲在古老的皮肤上磨来蹭去。他的身体总是被各式疼痛折磨——这正是身为无尽者的宿命——而这种持续的摩擦让他一挠痒就会掉下一块块血肉。再也不会长回来的血肉。##埃瑟尔走过一座天桥时朝下瞥了一眼。向下数里，越过漂浮的岛屿与游移的云层，他看见一片片人工灯火——在地表世界的幽暗中悸动明灭。亲爱的读者，因为这个故事发生在第一次尸骸十字军时期，那时余烬人的城市还繁盛着。##埃瑟尔的坐骑停了下来。他抬头望见一座简陋的住所，建了不过几十年。炊烟从烟囱升起，暴露了里面凡人居民的踪迹。阿尔德勋爵会很满意的。##他翻身下马，拔出剑。虽然肚子咕咕作响，但他今天不能进食。新鲜的肉要先运回战团，口粮再统一分配。话虽如此，埃瑟尔早已怀疑他的勋爵是故意让部队饿着肚子的，好扰乱他们的判断、滋养他们的怒火。##那扇门在他的体重下轻而易举地变形了。一个男孩站在他面前，满脸茫然。埃瑟尔的剑轻轻滑入男孩的肋间，他软倒在地板上。某处，一个女人尖叫起来；近来这声音再熟悉不过了。##一个老人冲出来，用长矛刺穿了埃瑟尔。这让他有些恼火，因为他的胸口早已千疮百孔，大风天里还会呜呜作响。埃瑟尔掐住那人的喉咙，举起剑准备劈下。##但有什么东西拦住了埃瑟尔。他注视着那个人，体内有什么东西搅动起来。是那双眼睛里的什么；就像望进一面雾蒙蒙的镜子。难道是？##老人已停止了挣扎，因为同样的遥远回忆也在他心中浮现了。##老人咽了口唾沫，结结巴巴，最终嘶哑地吐出："父亲？"##埃瑟尔的手松开了。他放下那个人，放下了剑。一种恐惧将他吞没；那是他许久以来感受到的第一丝真实的情感。##还没等他明白发生了什么，一个女人已捡起他的剑砍下了他的头颅。世界砰地一声迎面撞来。他躺在那里，缓缓地眨着眼，任由那家人把他的身体剁成碎块。##他们把埃瑟尔埋在花园里，作为某种受之有愧的敬意。他一动不动地绷着脸，好让他们以为自己真的死了；他太懦弱，不敢有别的举动。##那是个浅浅的坟，森林的声响渗进土里滤到他耳边。当罪疚与羞耻退潮，他感到一种安宁；离他曾深爱的人如此之近。家人。儿子。他在泥土中无声地念着这些字，听众是蠕虫与虫豸。##但某一天（或者某夜，他分不清），他从浑浑噩噩的麻木中醒来，耳边是烈焰与尖叫。他听着哭喊、屠杀、恐惧；但随后的寂静更糟。##然后，人声；脚步；一道炫目的光。他的头发被人从土里拽出，是阿尔德勋爵亲手把他高高拎起。那混蛋的狞笑像一道伤口，从左耳咧到右耳。##"哟哟，"他说，"咱们这儿捞着什么了？"##埃瑟尔越过他的勋爵，望向远处还在冒烟的房子。三具新鲜的尸体排得整整齐齐。##

English: Official Record of Junior Commitologist Pugh
Chinese: 初级提交学官皮尤的官方记录

English: To whom it may concern, ##My name is Gavelkind Pugh, Junior Commitologist of the Guild of Machinists and Acting Royal Factor of the township of Progress.##Let this document serve as my official record of the town's final days and of my role in them, so that my colleagues may judge and learn. ##I shall pick up directly from Senior Commitologist Pinsky's last report to the King on Month 1, Day 31. Shortly after invoking emergency powers and putting the town under quarantine, S.C. Pinsky was himself taken by the Corruption, leaving me -- at the unripe age of 23 -- as the most senior and indeed only Machinist at the scene. ##At that time, I was certain that the Clockwork King would be preparing a rescue force, despite my senior's warnings to the contrary. I therefore reasoned that the survival of Guild personnel, possessing vital intelligence about this new form of Corruption, was paramount. To that end, I ordered the Militia to fortify the factory compound and bar access to the townsfolk, lest they bring the curse within our walls. ##Initial dissent was peaceful. A lathe operator named Zayneb Muir negotiated with me through the fence, detailing the citizens' impromptu quarantine methods. From early reports of the Corruption I knew that these safeguards were fatally incomplete, but I did not share this information because it had been restricted by the King, and I feared punishment if I survived. ##By halfway through Month 2 the citizens were desperate, having been progressively forced to abandon most of the town. There were several attempts to break into our compound, and I authorised our acting Militia captain -- in truth a young corporal -- to take all necessary measures. Meanwhile, I continued my attempts to establish contact with the King, such as by modifying the factory's exhaust chimneys to flare at regular intervals. ##On Month 2, Day 41, I learned there would be no rescue. Its Majesty had finally pondered S.C. Pinsky's message, and its new orders -- still addressed to him -- were to stay put and prevent anyone escaping. Since I have nothing left to lose by being frank, I will plainly state that this plunged me into a deeper despair than I have ever known. When the townsfolk at last battered down our doors, they found me in the foreman's office, trying to summon the will to drive a sword into my guts. ##It was Citizen Muir who saved my life. In her own robust fashion, she persuaded me that I was better off using my knowledge of cipheristry and the King's machines to help refortify the compound, and hold out as long as we could. I was relieved to shrug off my now purely theoretical authority and submit to a more collective form of leadership. To our credit, we lasted another 35 days. ##On the 36th day our fences bubbled like boiling water, and every word we tried to say came out as incomprehensible song. The Corrupted swarmed in and most of us died, including Citizen Muir. The survivors retreated to the main gunnery tower, leaving behind the bulk of our uncontaminated food. ##Several conclusions follow from these events. Firstly, I recommend that Fiontann Pinsky and Zayneb Muir be posthumously named Heroes of the Clockwork Kingdom, and that the citizens of Progress collectively receive the Royal Commendation for Patriotic Labour. Secondly, I recommend that a committee be formed to investigate the reasons for this disaster, and that all Junior Machinists receive additional training in emergency leadership.##Finally, I implore my colleagues to ponder the wider lessons of my fate. Given the limited information available to me at the time, my decisions were understandable; yet I am haunted by what might have been. With the factory compound's extensive cipher wardings, it is possible -- albeit unlikely -- that a large group of untainted townsfolk could have held out against the curse long enough to be rescued. Where would we be now, had I trusted them earlier? Or if we had trusted all citizens with proper information from the beginning? The fall of Progress must prompt us to question every assumption we take for granted. ##The Corrupted are hammering now on our walls and shutters. Our voices are drowned by the cacophony of hundreds of limbs on metal. I must forego further reflections and take my place among the defenders, to fight and die together as citizens of Progress.##Long live the King! ##Gavelkind Pugh, Junior Commitologist ##Century 0, Year 24, Month 3, Day 29
Chinese: 致相关人士: ##我叫加维尔金德·皮尤,机械师公会初级提交学官,进步镇代理皇家事务官。##谨以此文书作为我对该镇最后时日、以及我在其中所扮演角色的正式记录,以便同僚们评判与借鉴。##我将直接从高级提交学官平斯基呈交国王的最后一份报告讲起,即1月31日。在启用紧急权力、将全镇隔离检疫后不久,S.C.平斯基本人也被腐化夺走,留下我——年仅23岁、尚且稚嫩——成为现场资历最深、实际上也是唯一的机械师。##当时,我确信发条王正在筹备救援力量,尽管我的上曾警告并非如此。因此我推断,掌握着这种新型腐化重要情报的公会人员能否存活,是压倒一切的大事。为此,我下令民兵加固厂区、禁止镇民入内,以免他们把诅咒带进我们的围墙。##最初的不满是和平的。一位名叫扎伊娜布·缪尔的车床工隔着栅栏与我交涉,详述了市民们自发采取的隔离方法。根据关于腐化的早期报告,我知道这些防护措施有致命的疏漏,但我没有分享这一信息,因为它已被国王列为机密,而我担心自己若活下来会受惩罚。##到2月过半,市民们已陷入绝望,被迫逐步放弃了镇子的大部分地区。发生了数次冲击厂区的尝试,我授权我们的代理民兵队长——实际上是个年轻下士——采取一切必要措施。与此同时,我继续尝试与国王建立联系,比如改造工厂的排烟烟囱,使其定期喷焰。##2月41日,我得知不会有救援了。国王陛下终于斟酌了平斯基的口信,而它的新命令——收件人仍是平斯基——是原地驻守,不许任何人逃脱。既然我已坦白无妨,无妨直言:这让我陷入了我此生所知最深的绝望。当镇民们终于撞开我们的大门时,他们发现我在工头办公室里,挣扎着鼓起勇气,想把一柄剑刺进自己的肚腹。##是缪尔公民救了我。她以她特有的豪爽方式说服了我:与其寻死,不如用我对密文学和国王机器的了解帮助加固厂区,能撑多久撑多久。我如释重负地卸下了我那如今纯属理论的权威,服从一种更集体的领导。值得我们自豪的是,我们又撑了35天。##第36天,我们的围栏像滚水一样鼓泡,我们说的每一句话都变成了无法理解的歌声。腐化者蜂拥而入,我们大多丧命,包括缪尔公民。幸存者撤往主炮塔,丢下了我们大部分未受污染的存粮。##从这些事件中可以得出几条结论。第一,我建议追授菲奥南·平斯基和扎伊娜布·缪尔"发条王国英雄"称号,并集体授予进步镇市民"爱国劳动皇家嘉奖"。第二,我建议成立委员会调查这场灾难的成因,并让所有初级机械师接受额外的紧急领导力培训。##最后,我恳请我的同僚们思考我的命运所蕴含的更深层的教训。以我当时掌握的有限信息,我的决定情有可原;但我仍被"本可以如何"所纠缠。凭借厂区完备的密文护符,一群未受污染的镇民——虽然可能性不大——或许本可以顶住诅咒,撑到获救之时。若我早一点信任他们,我们会走到哪一步?若我们从一开始就让所有公民掌握真实的信息,又会怎样?进步镇的陷落必须促使我们质疑每一个想当然的假设。##腐化者此刻正在捶打我们的围墙和窗板。我们的声音被数百只肢体敲击金属的喧嚣淹没。我必须停止进一步的沉思,去和守卫者并肩作战,作为进步镇的公民一同战斗、一同赴死。##国王万岁!##加维尔金德·皮尤,初级提交学官##0世纪24年,3月29日

English: Dispatch No. 533: WHAT IS CORRUPTION?
Chinese: 第533号急报:何为腐化?

English: WE at the Royal Dispatch have lately received many Letters enquiring as to the Nature & Causes of the Corruption. That this vile Curse, having stolen or otherwise marr'd the Lives of so many good Citizens, should remain a Subject of Confusion is only natural; & therefore we are pleased to present this Essay by a loyal Servant of the Clockwork King, upon that very Question.   ##*   *   *  ##My fellow Citizens,  ##As we celebrate the 30th anniversary of our beloved Clockwork Kingdom, the recent Evacuations in Cloudpine Oblast have once again put the Question of Corruption uppermost in every patriotic Citizen's mind. When I meet ordinary Subjects of our King, I am often asked: where did it come from? How can we stop it? Who is to blame?  ##There is nothing disloyal about these Questions. The Guild of Machinists has been forthright about the scale of this Crisis, & the Actions required from every Citizen in order to defeat it. Yet in devoting our Energies so wholly to the front line of the Battle, I recognise that we have neglected the vital Task of enumerating our Rationale to the People, allowing Misconceptions to percolate unchallenged.  ##Some claim that the Machinists do not truly understand the Causes of the Corruption. Others propose that it stems from Faults in the workings of our King, or from errant Counsel by Its Majesty's Advisers. There are even Whispers that we Machinists created it, as a Plot to reduce surplus Population, excuse further Tyranny, or some other nefarious Design.  ##I do not fear to print these Claims, for I believe that with the correct Knowledge our People will easily recognise what they are: pure Nonsense, in some cases emanating from deliberate Deceptions by Enemies of the Realm. While much remains unknown about the Corruption, these basic Facts can be stated plainly.  ##First, all Citizens have my solemn Oath, under the gaze of our Sovereign, that neither Its Majesty nor the Machinists' Guild has ever proposed, attempted, or designed to inflict the Corruption on any person or place; nor will we ever do so.  ##Corruption is nothing less than a Canker in the body of Reality itself, in which those base Elements that comprise our Existence are twisted, as a well-ordered Crowd may be agitated into an unruly Mob, to Riot & Discord. Conversely, Its Majesty's workings are based on the perfect Symmetry of the True Language. By definition, such a Monarch -- continuously audited by some of the finest magical minds in the Skyrealms over thirty years of governance -- cannot give rise to such profound Disunion.  ##Then what can? One answer, repeatedly confirmed by Guild studies and the King's own oracular Powers, is the World Rend, from which the Skyrealms remain in Recovery. Among its lingering effects are numerous Anomalies where natural laws such as Momentum, Causality, or the Conservation of Substance do not consistently pertain.  ##A second answer lies within our own human Frailties. Most Citizens are familiar with the first Maxim of Apostatic philosophy: that Belief precedes Divinity. That is, it is our own Minds -- our Hopes, our Fears, our Fancies -- that gives rise to the Gods & Spirits that we banished during the War of Theistic Liberation. By this same Principle, if our minds are riven by Turmoil or clouded by Doubt, we darken & corrupt what is around us.   ##The power of our King is ever-advancing, but not infinite, & in certain cases can be impeded by such factors. When this happens, the intended Transfigurations are left incomplete, putting Reality in Contradiction with itself. It is this interruption of Its Majesty's proper operation -- the unresolved clash between Order & Chaos -- which spawns Corruption. Hence, alas, the fault is not in Its Majesty but in ourselves, and in this fallen World we inhabit.  ##Long live the Clockwork King!  ##-- Austell Cicerone, Chief Summoner of the Guild of Machinists  ##*   *   *  ##THIS WEEK'S COMMENDATIONS  ##The Citizens' Literacy Commendation is awarded every Fortnight to the first six Readers to send a correct Solution to our regular Word Puzzle.   ##For Dispatch No. 532 (pub. Century 0, Year 29, Month 2, Day 48), the Winners, in order of Receipt, were as follows:  ##- F.P. Kwarteng #- Amrit Kaur #- O. Myshkin #- Dmitri Poskov #- J. Jaczemir #- E.G. Chinese: 敝报《皇家急报》近日收到大量来信,询问腐化的性质与成因。这可憎的诅咒夺走或损毁了许多善良公民的生命,而它至今仍是一个令人困惑的话题,这实属自然;因此,我们很高兴呈上发条王的一位忠仆就这一问题撰写的文章。##*   *   *##我的公民同胞们:##在我们庆祝心爱的发条王国建国三十周年之际,云杉州最近的疏散行动,再次把腐化的问题推到了每一位爱国公民心头的最前端。当我见到我们国王的普通臣民时,经常被问道:它从何而来?我们如何阻止它?该怪谁?##这些问题毫无不忠之处。机械师公会已坦率说明这场危机的规模,以及每位公民为战胜它所需的行动。然而,由于我们把全部精力都投入了战斗的最前线,我承认我们忽视了一项重要任务:向人民阐明我们的道理,任由误解不受挑战地蔓延。##有人声称,机械师们并不真正了解腐化的成因。也有人提出,它源于我们国王运转中的故障,或国王陛下顾问的谬误进言。甚至有流言说,是我们机械师造出了它,作为削减过剩人口、为更多暴政开脱,或某种其他奸计的阴谋。##我不惧怕刊登这些说法,因为我相信,只要有正确的知识,我们的人民很容易认清它们的本质:纯粹的胡言,其中一些出自王国之敌蓄意的欺骗。关于腐化仍有许多未知,但以下基本事实可以明白无误地陈述。##第一,我以我们的君主注视之下的庄严誓言向全体公民保证:国王陛下和机械师公会从未提议、尝试或设计过对任何人或地方施加腐化;今后也绝不会这样做。##腐化无异于现实躯体中的一处溃疮:构成我们存在的那些低贱元素在其中被扭曲,就像一支秩序井然的人群被搅动成失控的暴民,陷入暴乱与纷争。相反,国王陛下的运转基于真言的完美对称。按定义,这样一位君主——三十年的统治中始终由天空领域最顶尖的魔法头脑审计——不可能造成如此深刻的分裂。##那么,什么能?一个答案,已被公会的研究和国王本人的神谕之力反复证实,就是世界撕裂——天空领域至今仍在其后恢复中。它的余波包括无数反常现象:动量、因果或质能守恒等自然法则在其中不再稳定成立。##第二个答案在于我们人类自身的弱点。大多数公民都熟悉背教哲学的第一条格言:信念先于神性。也就是说,正是我们自己的心智——我们的希望、恐惧与幻想——生出了我们在神权解放战争中放逐的神灵。依同一原理,若我们的心智被纷乱撕裂、被疑虑蒙蔽,我们就会污化、腐化周围的一切。##我们国王的力量不断精进,却并非无限,在某些情况下会受到这类因素的阻碍。一旦发生,预定的变形便半途而废,使现实陷入自相矛盾。正是这种对国王陛下正常运转的打断——秩序与混沌之间未解的冲突——孳生了腐化。因此,唉,过错不在国王陛下,而在我们自己,以及我们所栖身的这个堕落世界。##发条王万岁!##——奥斯泰尔·西塞罗内,机械师公会首席召唤师##*   *   *##本周嘉奖##公民识字嘉奖每两周颁发一次,奖励最先就我们的常设字谜寄来正确答案的六位读者。##第532号急报(发表于0世纪29年2月48日)的获奖者,按来稿顺序为:##- F.P.夸藤加#- 阿姆里特·考尔#- 奥·米什金#- 德米特里·波斯科夫#- J.雅克泽米尔#- E.G.克罗赫斯特##出题人为高级释经官皮埃尔·科布利斯卡。##注:受庇佑的机械师公会成员可提交答案核对,但不在嘉奖之列。

English: A History of Kardova, by Beatrice Webb - 1411
Chinese: 卡尔多瓦史,比阿特丽斯·韦伯著——1411

English: How could a tiny island, known chiefly for its backwardness and incessant rain, transform itself in the space of nine years into a leading light of civilisation? The answer is one of the greatest stories of our age; and yet there has been no authoritative history of Kardova since Joan Toussaint's excellent treatise nearly two hundred years ago, which is now, through no fault of hers, missing some crucial developments.   ##Little is known about Kardova in ancient days. The island split off from Slev during the World Rend, and subsequently drifted in isolation for some centuries, during which time the largest part of it was destroyed in a collision with some airborne object. The survivors clung to a local god known to posterity only as the Den-Mother, described by the 12th-century traveller Al-Himarrh as zealously protective of her worshippers yet also bloodthirsty and vindictive. Even today, old songs and nursery rhymes hint at grotesque punishments meted out by her hierophants, such as execution by lightning strike or living burial.  ##Nevertheless, as the rest of the Skyrealms clawed their way out of the rubble and entered the Great Revival, Kardova's (at the time) high altitude attracted a growing contingent of astrologers, balloonists, and, later, aetherists, who used it as a staging ground for expeditions beyond the neuron stars. The discovery of ardentine ore in 1341 brought miners and geologists who settled and intermarried with the natives, along with dangerous new ideas and a greater consciousness of the outside world. The Coven of the Den-Mother cautiously welcomed this flood of industry in the hope of growing rich from the duties and taxes they could impose on it -- calculating, like so many rulers throughout history, that they could suppress the ensuing undercurrents of dissent and discontent through terror alone.   ##It was the coming of the God War in 1396 that finally dispelled this illusion. As apostatic rebellions erupted across the Skyrealms, the panicking priesthood embarked on a campaign of repression against suspected heretics, triggering strikes and mutinies among the miners. Attempts to suppress these by force only escalated the crisis, culminating with the overthrow of the Den-Mother's cultists in 1397 by a coalition of intellectuals and mineworkers. The fate of the goddess herself remains a mystery. ##Despite its mineral riches, the new Kardovan Republic was vulnerable and unstable, with numerous enemies within and without. And so, with the zealotry of a recent convert, and aided by enormous loans from Vena and Byonne -- which had both covertly sponsored the insurrection in the hope of gaining a new vassal -- it set about transforming itself into the workshop of the Union war effort.  ##The city of Istriksburg blossomed with enchanted foundries and manufactories, eagerly staffed by incoming refugees from across the Wikkanrule. These assembly yards soon grew so complex that they could only be managed with the aid of sophisticated cipher logic engines, constructing giant war machines capable of grappling face to face with gods and driving voidstone into their nuclei. By the end of the conflict they could build a 150-gun galleon from scratch in just three days, and a Schism-class sky fortress in two weeks.   ##Yet even before the war was over, a rift emerged over the shape of Kardova's future. The most radical voices, known as Machinists, talked of organising society around new engines of peace, making cipher magic predictable and accessible to all via mechanical science. Moderates, along with the wider Union nobility, saw this as a blueprint for chaos, while hardliners feared it would be a slippery slope back into god-worship. Four years later, formal ratification of the Treaty of Union remains mired in bitter disputes over mechanisation, intellectual freedom, and the repayment of war debt -- to say nothing of the latest incendiary proposals in Riova for an Apostatic Inquisition. Meanwhile, some geologists predict that Kardova's famed mineral veins may run dry within a few decades, potentially depriving it of a major bargaining chip.  ##Today, from my balcony above a teahouse in Istriksburg, I watch the Kardovan miracle spiral ever deeper into discord. Already I have had to revise this volume several times over due to new upheavals. Last month, a Union curate and three Venan soldiers were killed by a mob while attempting to arrest a Machinist scholar. This month, the Alchemists' Guild -- itself split between Machinists and Vitalists -- vowed to dissolve the Provisional Diet by force if it appoints a new curate, prompting Vena to threaten to call in its debts. Many fear these factions will shortly come to greater violence; for having once overthrown their rulers, all Kardovans understand how easily it could happen again.  ##Above it all looms the inescapable dilemma: ''Who shall lead us?'' Not even the Machinists are united on this question. Yet the answer will undoubtedly reverberate across the Skyrealms, for not even the mightiest sultan can afford to ignore an island capable of creating such machines.   ##What will be the ultimate consequences of the Kardovan miracle? I suspect we have only seen the end of the beginning.
Chinese: 一座以落后和无休止的降雨闻名的小小岛屿,如何在九年之间蜕变为文明的灯塔?答案是本时代最伟大的故事之一;然而自近两百年前琼·图森那部杰出的论著以来,再无一部权威的卡尔多瓦史——而她的著作虽非其过,已缺失了一些关键进展。##关于远古时代的卡尔多瓦,我们所知甚少。这座岛在世界撕裂中从斯列夫分离出来,随后孤独漂流了数个世纪,其间它最大的一部分在一次与某飞行物的相撞中毁于一旦。幸存者们依附于一位后世仅知其名为兽穴之母的本地神祇;12世纪的旅人阿尔-希马尔描述她对信徒呵护备至,却又嗜血而记仇。即使在今天,古老的歌谣和童谣仍暗示着她的祭司施行的怪诞惩罚,如雷击处决或生埋。##尽管如此,当天空领域的其余部分从废墟中爬出、迈入大复兴时,卡尔多瓦(当时的)高海拔吸引了日益增多的占星家、气球飞行家,以及后来的乙太师,他们把这里当作前往神经元星之外探险的出发地。1341年阿登廷矿的发现引来了矿工和地质学家,他们在此定居、与当地人通婚,同时也带来了危险的新思想和对外部世界更清醒的认识。兽穴之母教团谨慎地欢迎这股产业洪流,指望从他们能征收的关税和捐税中发财——像历史上众多统治者一样盘算着,仅凭恐怖就足以压制随之而来的不满与怨愤的暗流。##1396年神之战的降临,终于击碎了这一幻梦。随着背教起义在天空各地爆发,惊慌失措的祭司团发动了一场针对异端嫌疑者的镇压运动,引发了矿工的罢工和哗变。武力镇压的尝试只会让危机升级,最终在1397年,兽穴之母的祭司被知识分子和矿工的联盟推翻。女神本人的命运至今成谜。##尽管矿产丰富,新的卡尔多瓦共和国依然脆弱不稳,内外强敌环伺。于是,怀着新皈依者般的狂热,并借助维纳和拜昂的巨额贷款——两国都曾暗中资助这场起义,指望收获一个新的附庸——它着手把自己改造为联盟战争机器的车间。##伊斯特里克堡城在魔法锻造厂和制造厂中绽放,急切地雇佣着来自维坎法之地各地的难民。这些装配场很快复杂到只有借助精密的密文逻辑引擎才能管理,建造出能与诸神正面搏斗、把虚空石钉入它们核心的巨型战争机器。到战争结束时,它们能在三天内从零造出一艘150炮大帆船,两周内造出一艘裂教级天空堡垒。##然而甚至在战争结束前,关于卡尔多瓦前途的裂痕就已出现。最激进的声音,人称机械师,谈论以新的和平引擎来组织社会,让密文魔法通过机械科学变得可预测、人人可用。温和派,连同联盟更广泛的贵族,视之为通往混乱的蓝图;强硬派则担心这是滑回神明崇拜的斜坡。四年之后,《联盟条约》的正式批准仍陷于关于机械化、思想自由和战争债务偿付的激烈争端——更别提里奥瓦最近提出的设立背教宗教裁判所的煽动性议案。与此同时,一些地质学家预言卡尔多瓦著名的矿脉可能在几十年内枯竭,从而失去一张重要的谈判筹码。##今天,从伊斯特里克堡一家茶楼楼上的阳台,我望着卡尔多瓦奇迹愈陷愈深的纷争。由于新的动荡,本书我已不得不修订了好几版。上个月,一名联盟助理牧师和三名维纳士兵在试图逮捕一位机械师学者时被暴民杀死。这个月,炼金师公会——其自身也分裂为机械师派与生机派——扬言,若临时议会任命新的助理牧师,就武力解散议会,逼得维纳威胁收回贷款。许多人担心这些派系很快会诉诸更大的暴力;因为既然推翻过一次统治者,所有卡尔多瓦人都明白,这种事再次发生有多么容易。##而在这之上,悬着一个无法回避的难题:''谁来领导我们?''在这个问题上,连机械师们也不团结。但答案必将响彻天空领域,因为再强大的苏丹,也无法忽视一个能造出这种机器的岛屿。##卡尔多瓦奇迹的最终结局会是什么?我怀疑,我们仅仅看到了开始的结束。

English: The Romance of the Scarab, Part IV, by Milo Casimir - 1431
Chinese: 圣甲虫罗曼史·第四部,米洛·卡西米尔著——1431

English: PROPERTY OF THE LIBRARY OF UNTRUTHS  ##BORROWED BY: Pierre Kobliska, Sr Interpreter #DUE: Year 23, Month 0, Day 30 (RETURNED)  ##BORROWED BY: Aphra Grey, Jr Interpreter #DUE: Year 25, Month 5, Day 0 (RETURNED)  ##BORROWED BY: Bela Morozov, Sr Summoner #DUE: Year 26, Month 4, Day 15  ##*   *   *  ##The slip she sat in, like the morning dew, #   Clung to her bosom; the cloth was perfumed gauze, #   Cleaving so closely to her nubile curves #   That the looking glass itself was lovesick for her. #   There lay fair Ghibelline in silken chains, #   Dripping her tears upon some subtle tome, #   Dreading the dawn, in which she was to wed #   The hated Melephon -- that man of sludge.  ##All day and night her nimble mind had raced #   Through every twist and runnel of this maze; #   Yet finding walls whichever way she turns, #   Inexorable duty on all sides, #   Now weeps, shuts out the world, and hopelessly #   Seeks consolation in philosophy.  ##Then, when her last oil is nearly spent, #   There sounds the thunderous beat of whirring wings,  #   And through her window climbs a limber shape #   Half flesh and blood, half chitin hard as bone, #   His pinions snapping back into their sheaths, #   The keen blade of his body honed by war, #   Casting his molten gaze upon her form; #   Who else but brave Gehenna's mortal foe, #   The Brazen Emir's champion, and the scourge #   Who smashed her father's fleet? Ay, that same beast #   Who'd paused upon the brink of the abyss #   Beneath the embers of a dying star #   To steal from her soft lips one hurried kiss: #   The Chosen of his God, bold Alcazar.   ##No coward was Ghibelline. Quick as a flash, #   She seized upon the folio where she'd stashed #   A last resort -- lest she at length decide #   To rob her suitor of his grudging bride -- #   Then draws her poisoned bookmark from its place #   And points the dagger, quivering, at his face.  ##At this the monster gave a savage laugh, #   and with a voice like magma, thus he snarled: #   ''Well met, my lady. Five days have passed #   Since my world shattered in your gentle grip. #   Five nights of sleepless agony; five deaths. #   The Scarab bids me conquer, and my oath #   Sealed by ancient magick, and my blood, #   No more permits me to defy Her will #   Than stop the rushing tides, or boil the sea. #   You are the ward of Her sworn foe; yet I #   Would sooner tear my left arm from its joint #   Than cause you grief, and sooner plunge myself, #   Writhing, howling, into the depths of hell #   Than live without your beauty one more day. #   Therefore I beg, if you are merciful #   As you are charming to my compound eye, #   Show pity on this wretch, and drive that blade #   Into this aching breast, that I may die.''  ##Silence itself stands still, afraid to breathe. #   Only the comely maiden's heaving chest, #   In counterpoint with the demon's heavy pant  #   Betrays the riot in our lovers' hearts. #   Yet as the poet reins the rebel mass #   By harnessing their wrath to higher cause, #   So Ghibelline's whirling mind espied a chance. #   Defying the Mute God with her eloquence, #   And stepping closer with each point he grants, #   She put to Alcazar these arguments:  ##''The Scarab longs for peace; is that not so?'' #   It is, growls he. She takes another step. #   ''Yet she is proud and jealous, quick to rage?'' #    She is. ''So if I slay her Chosen now, #   Then vengeance upon vengeance shall prevail #   Until your house and mine are burned to ash?'' #   Her face is close enough that his hot breath #   Burns on her cheeks, and only a finger's width #   Between their loins; he cannot but assent. #   ''Know you,'' she sighs, “that I am to be wed?'' #   A storm of grief upon his brow: ''To whom?'' #   ''To Melophon. My Cony is the price #   Of his alliance to my father's flag, #   And with him a mighty army even you #   Could not hope to oppose. But,'' she murmurs #   Laying her dainty hand upon his breast, #   ''If I am deflowered, I cannot wed. #   Forsooth, what else could better serve your God #   Than union 'twixt…?''   ##She does not reach the end. #   No sage was Alcazar, but nor a fool, #   For as he pondered each new postulate #   Woven together by our scholar's wit, #   So rosy-fingered understanding crept #   From out behind the overshadowing isle #   of duty, and bathed his mind in blazing light. #   As shackles from the weary convict's hands, #   Fall shattered on the searing crystal sands, #   Or as a raging river long contained #   O'ertops its dam and courses down the plain, #   So too his vows released him, and the beast, #   His feral passion utterly unleashed, #   Unfettered, uncontrollable, and unquenched, #   Fell ravenously on the tender wench.  ##In iron claws he clasps his willing prey, #   Tears off her nightgown, tosses it away, #   Then lifts her like a warlord with his thrall, #   And thrusts her helplessly against the wall,  #   Toppling candlesticks, scattering her combs #   While scripture falls forgotten on the stones, #   Ravishing with rough mandibles his prize, #   Compelling from her mouth such blissful cries, #   And Ghibelline, her legs around his spine #   Embracing sweet surrender, loss divine, #   The dark star of her heart in full eclipse, #   At last allows that tongue to part her lips, #   And press inside, and find what she has lost; #   Let loose the joyous dawn, and damn the cost.
Chinese: 虚言图书馆馆藏##借阅人:皮埃尔·科布利斯卡,高级释经官#到期:23年0月30日(已归还)##借阅人:阿芙拉·格雷,初级释经官#到期:25年5月0日(已归还)##借阅人:贝拉·莫罗佐夫,高级召唤师#到期:26年4月15日##*   *   *##她坐于薄纱之中,如晨间露水,#   紧贴胸前;那衣料是熏香的云纱,#   如此贴合她柔嫩的曲线,#   连镜子也为她害了相思。#   美丽的吉贝琳卧于丝绸的锁链,#   泪珠滴落在某部精深的典籍上,#   畏惧着黎明——她将于黎明出嫁,#   嫁给那可憎的梅勒丰——烂泥般的男人。##她的机敏心智日夜奔驰,#   穿行这迷宫的每一道弯、每一条沟;#   却无论转向何方都碰壁,#   不可推卸的责任四面包围,#   于是哭泣,闭绝人寰,绝望地#   在哲学中寻求慰藉。##而后,当她的灯油将尽,#   嗡鸣双翼的雷鸣般的鼓点响起,#   一个柔韧的身影爬入她的窗,#   半是血肉,半是硬如坚骨的甲壳,#   翼刃咔哒收回鞘中,#   身躯的利锋经战争磨砺,#   熔金般的目光投向她的身姿;#   除了英勇革赫纳的凡间死敌,#   黄铜埃米尔的勇士、那击溃#   她父亲舰队的灾星,还能是谁?啊,正是那头兽——#   曾在一颗垂死之星的余烬下、#   深渊的边缘停驻,#   只为从她柔软的唇间偷走一个仓促的吻:#   他神明拣选之人,无畏的阿尔卡萨。##吉贝琳绝非懦夫。说时迟那时快,#   她抓起那册夹着最后一着——以防她终究决定#   从求婚者手里夺回那位勉强的新娘——的书页,#   抽出淬毒的书签,#   将匕首颤巍巍地指向他的脸。##怪物闻此放声狂笑,#   以岩浆般的声音咆哮道:#   ''幸会,我的夫人。五天已过,#   自我的世界在你温柔的掌中粉碎。#   五个不眠痛楚之夜;五次死亡。#   圣甲虫命我征服,我的誓言#   由古老的魔法与我的鲜血封印,#   再不容我违逆她的旨意,#   犹如无法拦住奔涌的潮汐,煮沸大海。#   你是她誓死之敌的被监护人;可我#   宁可把左臂从关节上生生撕下,#   也不愿让你受半分委屈,宁可把自己#   扭曲哀号着掷入地狱深处,#   也不愿再见不到你的美丽一日。#   因此我求你,若你也如你对我这只复眼#   那般迷人一般仁慈,#   就可怜可怜这苦命人,把那柄刃#   刺进这颗痛楚的胸膛,让我死吧。''##寂静屏息,不敢呼吸。#   只有美人起伏的胸膛,#   与魔物沉重的喘息互相应和,#   泄露了这对恋人心中的风暴。#   然而正如诗人勒住反叛的群氓,#   把他们的愤怒套上更高的事业,#   吉贝琳旋转的心智觅得了一线生机。#   她以雄辩违逆缄默之神,#   随着他的每一个让步而步步逼近,#   向阿尔卡萨抛出这些论点:##''圣甲虫渴望和平;不是吗?''#   是,他咆哮。她又上前一步。#   ''可她傲慢善妒,动辄暴怒?''#   是。''那么,若我此刻杀了她拣选的人,#   复仇之上再添复仇,#   直到你的家族与我的家族烧成灰烬?''#   她的脸近得能感到他灼热的呼吸#   烧着她的脸颊,两人腰腹间#   只隔一根手指的距离;他不得不承认。#   ''你可知道,''她叹息,''我将出嫁?''#   一场悲伤的风暴涌上他的额头:''嫁给谁?''#   ''嫁给梅勒丰。我的贞洁是他#   与我父亲结盟的代价,#   连同他麾下连你也无法指望#   抗衡的雄师。但是,''她低语,#   把纤手按上他的胸膛,#   ''若我失了贞洁,便嫁不成了。#   说真的,还有什么比……的结合,#   更能侍奉你的神明……?''##她没能说完。#   阿尔卡萨不是圣贤,却也不是蠢货,#   因为当他思量着我们这位才女#   巧手编织的每一条新命题,#   玫瑰色手指的领悟便悄然爬出#   责任那座遮天蔽日的岛屿背后,#   以烈焰之光沐浴他的头脑。#   如同镣铐从疲惫囚徒的腕上#   粉碎在灼热的水晶沙上,#   又如久被拦蓄的怒江#   漫过堤坝,奔涌直下平原,#   他的誓言同样解开了他;那头兽,#   野性的激情彻底决堤,#   不受束缚,无法遏制,无法浇灭,#   贪婪地扑向那柔弱的姑娘。##他以铁爪擒住甘愿的猎物,#   撕下她的睡裙,抛到一旁,#   再像挟着战利品的军阀般将她抱起,#   把她无助地抵上墙壁,#   烛台翻倒,梳子四散,#   经卷被遗忘,跌落在石上,#   他用粗粝的口器蹂躏他的奖品,#   逼出她口中极乐的叫喊,#   而吉贝琳,双腿环着他的脊背,#   拥抱着甜蜜的缴械,神圣的沦陷,#   她心中的暗星全然蚀没,#   终于任那张舌头分开她的唇,#   探入其中,寻回她失落之物;#   放纵这欢愉的黎明,管他代价几何。

English: VOLUME I: THE BASICS OF SIXFOLD  ##Fiana Constanza, the inventor of Sixfold cipher, was so overcome by its terrible beauty that she jumped to her death from the edge of Byonne's main island in the 173rd year Ante Rex. Acheron Twisp, the Lundelese scholar who first translated & assembled Constanza's work for modern eyes, likewise died by his own hand in Century 0, Year 8. Now it is our turn to study Sixfold cipher.  ##This book shall furnish you with all you need to follow in the footsteps of these illustrious forebears. The authors hope that it might also aid you in diverging from their path where you consider it prudent.  ##If you too should perish by your own hand after reading this book, we pray you dispatch a letter of complaint, or perhaps make a personal visit, to our beloved publisher Dr Ecgbehrt Prust, whose address is given in the front matter of this volume, & who, we have no doubt, will be more than happy to make due recompense.  ##Now, without further ado, our lesson begins.  ##Our ancestors believed in a harmonious cosmos, where all things danced in unison to the ''music of the spheres''. Current scholarship suggests that this music is more like the cacophony of a million howling dogs.  ##As you know, the true structure of cipher language is an incomprehensibly intricate and perhaps infinite set of relations between ontologically unstable entities known as glyphs. For mortal beings, exposure to this cosmic bedlam may cause lethargy or headaches at best and seizures, brain haemorrhages, dematerialisation, or malign apotheosis at worst.  ##Since most mortal scholars prefer to avoid this, it is usually necessary to 'translate' cipher glyphs and their relationships to each other into a clearer and less volatile scheme known as a cipher transposition, which ignores almost all relationships between glyphs in order to focus on just a few.  ##You may already be familiar with common transpositions such as magic circles, mandalas, hermetic sigils, and the Metachromatic Scale. However, the intricacy and relative inflexibility of these structures presents a high barrier to using them in mechanical devices.   ##Constanza's breakthrough was to further 'translate' existing transpositions into an abridged yet adaptable dialect that did not depend on rigid geometric or tonal forms. Her solution was to distil Byonne's standard glyph alphabet into just six symbols that could be used to invoke components of a standard transposition, which in turn would invoke the True Language.   ##Many scholars scoffed at Constanza's hope of making cipher magic safe enough for layfolk to study. Almost all considered it impossible to forge mechanical components precise enough to perform such rituals without a human caster. They were wrong.  ##To print the Six Letters of Fiana Constanza here would risk producing a magic book, rather than a mere book of magic. Yet by virtue of the mystical arithmetic that connects these letters to their intermediary transpositions, they are largely equivalent in operation to the common numerals 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, which we shall henceforth use as a shorthand. Eager students may fill out the coupon on our final page and post it to our publisher to receive an example of the letters on specially warded vellum.   ##Study these letters. Study them well. Study them until your eyesight fades and your head feels stuffed with fur, until your cheeks are gaunt and your loved ones ask with genuine concern whether you are in good health, and you answer with what cheer you can muster that you are quite all right, thank you, but they are not convinced and talk of you amongst themselves in soft, worried voices, and go silent when you enter the room.  ##You will know you have succeeded when you start to perceive these letters everywhere: in the scudding of the clouds, in the frothing of your ale, in the laughter of your friends, in the whispering of the neuron stars, in the lights you see when you close your eyes, and in your dreams.
Chinese: 第一卷:六重密文基础##六重密文的发明者菲亚娜·康斯坦扎,被它可怖的美所慑,于王前纪173年从拜昂主岛的边缘一跃而下,殒命。阿刻戎·特威斯普,最早把康斯坦扎的著述翻译并整理、以供今人阅读的伦德尔学者,同样在0世纪8年自戕身亡。如今,轮到我们来研习六重密文了。##本书将为你提供循着这些杰出先行者足迹所需的一切。笔者们也希望,在你认为审慎之处,它能助你偏离他们的道路。##若你读罢此书也自戕身亡,我们恳请你写一封投诉信,或干脆登门拜访,献给我们敬爱的出版商埃格伯特·普鲁斯特博士——他的地址见本书卷首——我们毫不怀疑,他一定非常乐意作出应有的补偿。##闲话少叙,课程开始。##我们的先祖相信宇宙和谐,万物随''天球音乐''齐声共舞。当代学术研究表明,这音乐更像百万只狂吠之犬的喧嚣。##如你所知,密文语言的真实结构,是一组被称为符文的、本体论上不稳定的实体之间令人无法理解的错综复杂、或许无穷无尽的关系。对凡人而言,接触这宇宙的混沌,轻则昏沉头痛,重则癫痫发作、脑出血、物质化消解,甚至恶性成神。##既然大多数凡间学者宁愿避开这些,通常就有必要把密文符文及其相互关系'翻译'成一种更清晰、更稳定的体系,称为密文置换;它几乎忽略所有符文间的关系,只聚焦于寥寥数个。##你可能已熟悉常见的置换,如魔法阵、曼陀罗、赫尔墨斯印记和变色音阶。然而,这些结构的繁复与相对僵化,为在机械装置中使用它们设置了极高的门槛。##康斯坦扎的突破,是把既有置换进一步'翻译'成一种精简而灵活的方言,不再依赖僵硬的几何或音律形式。她的方案,是把拜昂的标准符文字母表蒸馏成仅仅六个符号,用以调用一档标准置换的组件,而后者再调用真言。##许多学者讥笑康斯坦扎想让密文魔法安全到外行也能研习的宏愿。几乎所有人都认为,造出足够精密、能在无人施法者的情况下执行此类仪式的机械部件,是不可能的。他们错了。##在此印出菲亚娜·康斯坦扎的六个字母,恐有制出魔法之书、而非仅仅魔法书籍之虞。但凭借把这些字母与其中介置换相连的神秘算术,它们在运作上大体等价于常见数字0、1、2、3、4、5,我们此后将以此作为简写。好学的学生可填写本书末页的优待券,寄给我们的出版商,以领取印于特制护符羊皮纸上的字母样本。##研习这些字母。用心研习。研习到视力衰退、头脑像塞满毛絮,研习到双颊凹陷、亲友们真心实意地询问你是否安康,而你强打精神回答说我很好、谢谢,可他们并不相信,彼此用轻柔而忧虑的声音议论你,并且在你走进房间时陷入沉默。##当你开始在处处看见这些字母时:在疾行的云里,在你的麦酒泡沫里,在朋友的笑声里,在神经元星的低语里,在闭上眼睛时看见的光里,在梦里——你就知道自己成功了。
